about: How Odia is typed in Latin letters (these fitted weights describe chat; half of the transliterator's synthetic pairs are spelled from them, the other half from the fitted weights): native word -> canonical romanisation (the first spelling of every slot), weighted chat spellings, and the skeleton folds the romanised lookup keys on. Read by training/mlkb/langs/romanisation.py; the weights are fitted to Aksharantar ori's manual valid rows (training/mlkb/langs/calibrate.py). Each table maps a letter (or a letter + nukta, or a conjunct) to [spelling, weight] options, canonical first. Started from Bengali's table: the two scripts are laid out alike.

skeleton.about: Applied to typed Latin and to the canonical romanisation alike: lowercase a-z only; the longest `replace` key at each position (else `letters`, else the letter itself); a symbol equal to the one before it is dropped (doubled letters); then a final vowel in `dropFinal` after a consonant is dropped.

looseSpelling.about: Which typed spellings spell a word out, for ranking (the engine's Romanisation::relaxed): `singles` read a letter as another, `pairs` read two letters in a row as one, `collapse` letters count once however often they repeat. Vowel length only: Odia keeps d and t apart (ଦ, ତ).

notes.inherent: The inherent vowel is said (a rounded a, near o) and typed a, sometimes o (କଥା katha, ଘର ghara / ghar). Odia drops no inherent vowel inside a word in speech, so there is no schwaDeleted list. At the end of a word it is typed or left out (ଓଡ଼ିଶା odisha, ଭୁବନେଶ୍ୱର bhubaneswar), so the skeleton drops a final a.
notes.letters: ଯ is j (ଯାଇ jai) and ୟ y (ଭୟ bhaya, ହୋଇଯାଇ); the -ya sign (virama + ଯ) is y (ବ୍ୟବସାୟ byabasaya). ବ is b; the -wa sign ୍ୱ is w or v (ସ୍ୱାମୀ swami). ଶ ଷ ସ are all said s and typed s or sh. ଡ଼ is said r and typed d or r (ଓଡ଼ିଆ odia, ବଡ଼ bada / bara); the tables put the commoner first, and the other spelling reaches the word through the transliterator. ୃ is ru (କୃଷ୍ଣ krushna, ସଂସ୍କୃତି sanskruti) or ri. କ୍ଷ is ksh, khy or x (ଲକ୍ଷ୍ମୀ laxmi), ଜ୍ଞ gy, jn or gn.
notes.anusvara: ଂ is n, ng or m (ସଂସ୍କୃତି sanskruti, ଏବଂ ebang / ebam). The skeleton folds ng to n, so ଏବଂ typed ebang finds the word whose key ends in n (calibration skeleton 86.8% to 87.3%); the price is that ଙ୍ଗ words share keys with ନ words. mb and mp fold to nb and np. A final candrabindu ଁ is written or not (ନାହିଁ nahin / nahi), so optionalFinals names it.
notes.skeleton: Aspirates fold to their plain letters, sh and chh/ch to s and c, z to j, f to p, v and w to b, q and x to k; aa, ee and oo to a, i and u; ou to au, oi and ae to ai (ଲଗାଇ lagai / lagae), ay to e (Aksharantar's annotators often typed େ as ay: ନେତ୍ରୀ naytri, calibration skeleton 85.2% to 86.8%), ng to n. A final a after a consonant is dropped.
notes.apostrophe: An apostrophe marks a dropped vowel (କ'ଣ kana / kan, ତା'ର tar). After a consonant it is spelled by apostropheVowel, as the vowel it stands for; after a vowel sign the walk skips it. The lexicon keeps it in the word.
